payload.report: The 20×14-cm² ulcer persisting for 3 years, combined with compound heterozygous COL7A1 splice-site mutations and immunofluorescence/electron microscopy showing type VII collagen and anchoring fibrils, establishes recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB). The healthy forearm patch and grafted area with preserved collagen are best interpreted as revertant/unaffected skin in RDEB, further supporting the diagnosis. Chronic non-genetic ulcer is essentially excluded by the genetic and microscopic findings. Secondary squamous cell carcinoma in the chronic wound cannot be fully ruled out because ulcer-margin histopathology is unavailable, but it remains a less likely concurrent concern requiring surveillance. Therefore, RDEB is the primary diagnosis.
